svg.title: Row storage makes you read everything
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing a CSV drawn as seven rows of eight shaded cells where seven of every eight cells are struck through as wasted, annotated that a sum over one column still reads all 663.3 megabytes; Parquet drawn as eight vertical strips whose widths are the real compressed column sizes from 69.5 megabytes for the timestamp down to 0.5 for a boolean, with only the 20.9 megabyte amount strip shaded; the same file split into ten row groups where nine are struck through in red because the footer statistics proved they cannot contain matching rows; and measured bars showing count star at 0.43 seconds on CSV against 0.0019 on Parquet, and sum of amount at 0.78 against 0.047.
svg.text: Row storage makes you read everything
CSV: rows. To read one column you read them ALL.
7 of every 8 bytes you read are thrown away
Parquet: columns. Read only what you asked for.
reads 20.9 MB of a 186.2 MB file (11.2%)
663.3 MB csv -> 186.2 MB parquet+snappy -> 141.6 MB zstd
and the footer lets it skip whole BLOCKS it never opens
remember week 14? A row group is a B-Tree
page for columns: skip the block, not the
226x on the count. 16x on the sum.
...and if you partition it too? -> Module 5
